class.name: YouTubeResolver
class.brief_description: Asynchronously resolves public YouTube media URLs using a native extractor.
class.description: Resolves YouTube watch, short, live, and embed links without downloading media. Extraction runs on a worker thread. YouTube JavaScript challenges use the bundled EJS scripts in an embedded QuickJS runtime; Python and external executables are not required. Available on threaded Windows, Linux/BSD, and Android builds. Web projects should use their browser playback path. Returned URLs expire and may require the returned HTTP headers and the same network identity used for resolution. This class ports the public YouTube playback subset of yt-dlp, not its complete site/extractor feature set. Login, cookies, DRM, proof-of-origin tokens, playlists, subtitles are not implemented.

method.name: cancel
method.description: Cancels an outstanding request. No completed signal is emitted for the cancelled request.

method.name: get_video_id
method.description: Returns the video ID from a supported HTTPS YouTube URL, or an empty string for unsupported input. An eleven-character video ID is also accepted.

method.name: is_resolving
method.description: Returns whether a resolution request is active.

method.name: resolve
method.description: Starts asynchronous resolution. The node must be in the scene tree. Returns [constant OK] when started, [constant ERR_BUSY] if already resolving, or an input/setup error. The result is delivered through [signal completed].

signal.name: completed
signal.description: Emitted on the main thread. On success, the result contains [code]url[/code], [code]selected_format[/code], [code]formats[/code], [code]http_headers[/code], [code]id[/code], [code]title[/code], [code]duration[/code], and [code]is_live[/code]. Separate inputs also include [code]audio_url[/code], [code]audio_format[/code], and [code]audio_http_headers[/code]; attach those to [member VideoStreamMedia.audio_file] and [member VideoStreamMedia.audio_http_headers]. Errors may include a [code]message[/code]. Resolving a URL does not guarantee the media endpoint will accept playback; authentication and service policy can still apply.
